s1.quote: Today, the wreck lies upright in warm, clear water with its deck at approximately 60m and the bottom at 70m. … especially heading towards the bow.

s2.quote: The shipwreck is upright on a sandy bottom at about 240' / 70m off Tinete Point … all dives are decompression dives which require the appropriate training and experience in extended range diving.

hazards.text: Current can be strong, especially toward the bow

summary.text: A US destroyer lost in 1943 that now sits upright off Florida Island near Tulagi. It is an extended-range decompression dive, with the deck near 60 m and sand near 70 m, so it suits experienced technical divers only.

s1.quote: The shipwreck is upright at a depth of 50' / 15.24m and encrusted with coral and home to marine life.

s2.quote: today rests in a sheltered bay in only 18m of water … we were blessed with 15m visibility

highlights.text: Cargo still in the hold; mast above water

s1.quote: Tulagi (less commonly known as Tulaghi) is a small island in Solomon Islands, just off the south coast of Ngella Sule.

notDiveSite.reason: A whole island and former capital, not a single dive site
